title: Diplomacy renounce (record)
description: A party ended a commitment unilaterally with a signed `renounce` press move to the counterparty (diplomacy-scenario.md §1.5, "the honest stab"). (2.5.0) A renounce is accepted only for an ACTIVE commitment (at least one clause still escrowed) that has not been renounced, sent privately to the counterparty; anything else is refused `commitment_unknown` (a renounce of an ended commitment is refused, never an accepted no-op). Clauses of a movement phase are released only if the renounce was delivered at or before the close of round R-1 of that phase (one full round of notice); a later renounce releases only later phases. `releases_from_phase` is the first movement phase whose clauses (of BOTH parties) settle `renounced`. (2.5.0) The renounce is recorded at the round close that delivers it, but settles nothing there: each released clause settles `renounced` at the ADJUDICATION of its phase, so the commitment stays `active` until the adjudication of its last covered phase. A renounce delivered in round R of a commitment's last covered phase releases nothing: its `releases_from_phase` lies after every covered phase (it may even lie after the game's final phase), and every remaining clause is judged `kept` or `broken` as usual. Renouncing is never an oracle failure.

releases_from_phase.description: The first movement phase released: the renounce's own phase when it was delivered by the close of round R-1, else the next movement phase. (2.5.0, widened) `S1909M` is allowed: it is the next movement phase after F1908M, produced by a renounce delivered in round R of F1908M, and it releases nothing. The same holds for any value after the commitment's last covered phase or after the game's final phase.

sig_mode.description: (2.4.0, B3a item 4) The renounce message's OWN attested mode, recorded by the engine when the message was accepted at its round close. Never inherited: a session-mode renounce of a key-mode commitment is recorded session. signing.md §7.4.

power.description: A standard-map power. Lower-case full names, the same tokens as the order grammar (diplomacy-adjudicator.md §1.1). Canonical order everywhere: alphabetical, as listed.

movement_phase.description: A movement phase id, e.g. S1902M. Years 1901..1908 (the longest horizon).

msg_id.description: Engine-assigned press message id `prs:<movement phase>:r<round>:<sender power>:<seq>`, seq = 1-based position in the sender's batch for that round. Never agent-chosen; deterministic, so an agent can predict its own ids (the offer signature covers the expected id).

cmt_id.description: Commitment id `cmt:<msg_id of the offer that was accepted>`. Exactly one commitment per accepted offer; a replayed accept returns the same id.

sig_mode.description: key = a detached Ed25519 JWS that verified against the sender's passport signing key (signing.md §7). session = attested only by the authenticated connection: the local CLI runner, or a table session of a development or test deployment; a hosted run or a production table never accepts it. Phase 9 evidence packs require key. A move's mode is its own; a commitment is key only if both its offer and its accept were key.
